items.title: Gucci Price Cuts Break Luxury's Biggest Taboo. Louis Vuitton Is Weighing It
items.summary: Forbes business analysis details Gucci's quiet price reductions (Padlock bag down 30% in France to EUR2,450; sneakers from EUR800 to EUR560-595; Mercato tote down 20-25%) after 13 consecutive quarters of falling sales, noting the luxury customer base shrank from roughly 400 million people in 2022 to about 340 million by 2025. Reports Louis Vuitton is weighing but has not followed Gucci's move, while third-quarter retail sales fell 9% on weaker China/Japan traffic; Kering frames the moves as a 'reset of price architecture.' Independent, critical-leaning coverage still circulating this week and directly relevant to SEA pricing expectations versus China/Japan softness.

items.title: Coach, Ralph Lauren defy China retail slump as badge of new cool
items.summary: Singapore's paper-of-record (syndicating a Bloomberg wire story) reports Coach and Ralph Lauren posted China sales up more than 30% for the quarter ending September, the same period Kering and LVMH labels logged double-digit China declines; frames younger Chinese shoppers as favoring practicality and value over heritage logo brands like Gucci and Balenciaga. Independent business-press coverage read by Singapore's financial/luxury audience that implicitly positions Gucci as losing share to accessible-logo competitors in the region's reference market.

items.source: Bangkok Post / Central Thailand retail (via Elle Thailand corroboration)
items.title: Gucci 'The Scent Show' launches at Central Thailand with 15% fragrance discount
items.summary: Central department store's Gucci storefront is running a fragrance promotion, 'The Scent Show,' from Nov 20-30 featuring Flora Gorgeous Magnolia, Guilty Elixir, Flora Gorgeous Jasmine and Flora Gorgeous Gardenia at a 15% discount. Descriptive retail/promotional coverage (activation, not editorial opinion) but notable as a discounting signal in Thailand that echoes the broader global Gucci price-cut narrative; corroborated independently by Elle Thailand's own listing of the same promotion.

items.source: Tom + Lorenzo (syndicated widely incl. Asia entertainment press)
items.title: Mariah Carey for Gucci's Holiday 2026 Ad Campaign
items.summary: Gucci's 2026 holiday campaign 'Gucci Gift,' directed by Harmony Korine and starring Mariah Carey soundtracked by 'All I Want for Christmas Is You,' continues generating fashion-press coverage into this week; Carey wears pieces from Gucci's new Butterfly collection inside a hotel set. Pure activation/campaign coverage with no independent critical angle, but a top-of-funnel visibility driver for Gucci across Asia and global holiday markets this week.

items.summary: Trade-press corroboration of the Bloomberg-originated China badge-of-cool story (Coach/Ralph Lauren outperforming while Kering/LVMH houses post double-digit China declines); included as a second independent source for the same competitive narrative given its continued syndication into this week's Straits Times republish, underscoring the story's sustained relevance to Gucci's positioning against accessible-luxury competitors in the region.

collection_notes: Today's fresh SEA-relevant pool is thin on locally-originated news: Thailand/Singapore/Philippines/Indonesia/Vietnam dailies (Thairath, Kompas, Detik, Philippine Daily Inquirer, VnExpress, The Star Malaysia) ran dry on fresh (within 7 days) Gucci-specific stories, so the news channel leans on globally-syndicated wire coverage reaching SEA readers (Straits Times republishing a Bloomberg China-retail piece, Forbes price-cut analysis) plus one genuinely SEA-local retail-promotion item (Central Thailand's 'Scent Show' discount, corroborated by Elle Thailand). Critical-angle searches surfaced a continuing, now-5-day-old independent narrative (Gucci price cuts vs Louis Vuitton's restraint; Coach/Ralph Lauren outperforming Kering/LVMH on China value-seeking consumers) that keeps circulating and was judged still within the acceptable freshness window; no brand-new critical story (store closures, scandal, quality complaint) specific to SEA surfaced today beyond this ongoing pricing narrative -- flagged as a case where 'critical searches' returned the same story rather than fresh negatives. Investigated and explicitly excluded as stale (>14 days or >1 year old): the 2018 Malaysian Gucci-loafer tribunal case, the 2023 Greenbelt 4 store-launch coverage, the May 2026 Gucci Cruise 2027 NY show (Anne Curtis/Davika Hoorne/Zhang Linghe), the October 2025 Billkin/Marina Bay Sands SS26 preview, and the April 2026 Jing Daily China-store-cuts piece. SNS/community checks (Pantip, Kaskus, Facebook -- all Priority-A per buzz_registry) were executed in Thai/Indonesian/English but again surfaced only evergreen consumer chatter and brand-owned promotional posts rather than organic fresh reaction threads; X search likewise yielded only non-quantifiable chatter (engagement metrics not retrievable, recorded null). Pool skews critical/mixed on the business-performance dimension (price cuts, China-share loss vs Coach/Ralph Lauren) balanced against light activation coverage (Mariah Carey holiday campaign, Scent Show promo); this should be read as the genuine state of SEA public conversation this cycle, not as pool manipulation in either direction.
